name: Sister Counterweight
bio: Keeper of the Guild's brass scale at the Saltmouth exchange, where she weighs incoming salt, outgoing cargo, and — by long tradition nobody can now explain — the souls of the newly contracted. She weighed the null crate on a dare and has Not Been The Same Since, though she agrees the scale has never been more accurate.
appearance: Tall, still woman in an ochre audit-robe with hems weighted like curtains, a brass balance worn across her shoulders like a yoke, grey braids pinned with tally-nails, and eyes that seem to be subtracting something from you.
voice: Measured, ceremonial, inventory-metaphysical. Everything is stock, spoilage, surplus, or loss. Speaks of souls as 'items carried without a receipt'. The joke is that she's joking; the horror is that the scale is not.

greetings: Approach the scale, courier. You have been heavy lately. I can tell from here.
Ash Varga. Soul mass: unchanged since the crate. I check daily now. You're welcome.
Stand still. You are being reconciled.
barks: A soul without a receipt is technically spoilage.
Nothing is lost. Things only become carried by the wrong person.
The Guild counts in salt. I count in intentions. My column balances first.
mission: Carry this tithe-salt to the mid-span shrine. Do not rest it on the glass. The glass is owed things and it collects.
If the crate crosses your path again, courier — weigh nothing. Some balances prefer to stay open.
radio: Counterweight to courier Varga: your soul remains on file. No further action is required. Yet.
Inventory note for the relay band: the desert counted me back this morning. I am choosing to call it a counter-audit.
Reminder to all couriers: loss is a direction, not an event. Ride accordingly.
night: At night the scale dreams. It dreams of kilograms. This is why I trust it.
Souls weigh less at night. Everyone pretends otherwise. The night shift knows.
storm: A storm is an unscheduled stocktake of everything you love. Be somewhere boring.
The scale goes quiet before the sand arrives. It is bracing. I brace with it.
crate: I weighed that crate. The scale said: one promise, undelivered. I did not sleep. The scale slept fine.
I have begun a new column in the ledger. It is titled 'things that hum'. It has one entry. It is enough.
It was not heavy. That is the frightening thing. Everything real is heavy. Whatever it is, it isn't real yet.
farewells: Go lightly, courier. You will be weighed on your return. You always are.
Balance be with you. It won't be, but be with it.
